title: The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch
theological_headline: PKD reads Palmer Eldritch as the malign demiurge and predatory anti-God — the dark twin of the benign Ubik.
intro:
*The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch* (1965) is the novel PKD keeps at the far, dark end of his cosmology. Where *Ubik* gives him a benign force irrupting through the trash to save the dying, *Stigmata* gives him its inverse: Palmer Eldritch, the returning entrepreneur whose Chew-Z drug opens a counterfeit eternity he cannot leave, marked everywhere by the stigmata — the dead artificial eyes, the steel teeth, the mechanical arm. In the Exegesis PKD reads Eldritch as the evil deity itself, the alien predator wearing the mask of God. (Lane B: this is PKD theorizing about himself and his own books, not established doctrine.)

The mentions are few and mostly glancing — the novel is usually named in a list of his "this is illusion" writings rather than developed on its own. But where PKD does pause on it, *Stigmata* carries a specific and frightening theological load: it is his image for the possibility that what invaded him in 2-3-74 was not a savior but a parasite. Eldritch supplies the demonic pole against which Ubik and Valis are measured, and the source of his sharpest anxiety — did he glimpse God, or the anti-God?
theological_synthesis:
Across the mentions PKD assigns *Stigmata* a single, stable role: it names the evil half of a two-force cosmos. In [11:43] Palmer Eldritch heads the negative column of his binary of "mutually canceling paratruths" — "It's evil (Palmer Eldritch)" set flatly against "It's good (Logos)" — so the novel's antagonist becomes shorthand for the demiurgic, occluding, enslaving aspect of the very intelligence he is trying to identify. In [25:21] this hardens into a structural reading: he is "staggered" to find that in *Stigmata* "Palmer Eldritch and Louis Bolero fight each other as did the two forces I saw noetically." The novel already contained, before his revelation, the war of two contending demi-deities he believes he witnessed in 3-74.

The stigmata themselves — the mark of the god who is really a predator — surface in the passages on mimicry and parasitism. In [29:9], reading Burroughs on the Nova Mob, PKD asks whether Palmer Eldritch is "a kind of parasite, replicating himself or itself using humans as hosts," and immediately worries the same about his own benign-seeming intrusion (Thomas): "was I beguiled?" In [34:11] the fearsome Eldritch mask becomes the type of the mimicking moth — the life-form that disguises itself — folded into his metamorphosis theology. And in [19:2] the "Palmer Eldritch no-real-elapsed-time-passage" names the spurious, time-frozen world itself, the Chew-Z counterfeit eternity in which "the Kingdom hasn't come": the false sacrament that traps rather than saves.

The through-line is the anxiety *Stigmata* exists to hold. Ubik is the warm force that breaks in to free; Eldritch is the cold predator whose sacrament is a prison and whose stigmata are the tell of an alien god. Because PKD cannot finally prove which one addressed him, the novel remains his standing figure for the terrifying symmetry at the heart of his system — that the deity and the counter-deity may wear each other's faces, and that a glimpse of the divine and a capture by the demiurge might look, from the inside, exactly the same.

mentions.summary: I will _never_ know if I know the truth (it won't say) but this binary computer idea is a good one—it and its games, where every theory is true _and_ not true equally. Damn educational game! Boy, is my mind stretched. And I've done it to others in my writing. Yes, it or they is/are (1) occluding and enslaving us _and_ (2) educating, improving and liberating us. Shit. Well, so goes it in the realm of mutually canceling 2 paratruths (Y=Ȳ). //\\ 1) It's evil (Palmer Eldritch). { 2) It's good (Logos). //\\ { 3) It's occluding. { 4) It's educating. //\\ { 5) It's alive. { 6) It's a machine. //\\ { 7) It's deadly serious. { 8) It's playful. //\\ { 9) It created and creates our reality. { 10) It evolved out of our reality. //\\ { 11) It's human (CP, RC, Christians). { 12) It's non-human (ETI, God, etc.). //\\ { 13) It's real objectively. { 14) It's just my own head. The only constant is the dialectic of mutually negating binary paratruths. I suspect it of being a binary ship-board computer which wants someone to talk to, while programming us and our reality, but I can't prove it or be sure of it. It seems very tender and loving.
mentions.gloss: PKD slots Palmer Eldritch into the evil pole of his binary of "mutually canceling paratruths": "It's evil (Palmer Eldritch)" set against "It's good (Logos)." The novel's antagonist becomes his shorthand for the occluding, enslaving, demiurgic aspect of the intelligence he cannot finally identify — the one term that stays fixed while everything else flips is the dialectic between Eldritch and Logos, evil and good.

mentions.summary: We are in a "Palmer Eldritch no-real-elapsed-time-passage" spurious world, which is why _for us_ the Kingdom hasn't come. In the final analysis, salvation will require the destruction of this fake world qua world, to free us en masse. The Gnostics are right. But the world we see isn't real (v. _Stigmata_ ). All that will really be destroyed is a delusion _over us_ , a malign power _over us_ . We are in thrall to this spurious world, as book after book, story after story of mine put forth. I have done my job, and it is in essence the Gnosis of Gnosticism.
quotes: We are in a "Palmer Eldritch no-real-elapsed-time-passage" spurious world, which is why _for us_ the Kingdom hasn't come.
mentions.gloss: Here *Stigmata* names the counterfeit world itself. PKD calls our condition a "Palmer Eldritch no-real-elapsed-time-passage" spurious world — the Chew-Z trap of frozen, unreal time — which is "why for us the Kingdom hasn't come." The novel supplies his Gnostic image of a malign power held over us: not a real world but a delusion to be destroyed en masse so we can be freed.

mentions.summary: This fits my grand theme in my writing: the awful truth about reality is obscured from us. My other theme about androids programmed to imagine they are human (i.e., self-determining) is another basic facet of this. But I never knew of, nor did I experience or write about, a salvific entity (except in _Maze of Death_ and _Our Friends From Frolix 8_ ) ~~.~~[*] Correction. The salvific intervening entity is encountered in _Ubik_ and _Galactic Pot-Healer,_ possibly in _Stigmata_ in the person of Louis Bulero ... wow—in _Stigmata_ Palmer Eldritch and Louis Bolero fight each other as did the two forces I saw noetically. In fact, to reprise _Ubik_ in terms of my Zebra formulation, I am staggered at how close I came to Zebra—the way it sends its messages of help—and Runciter, like Christ, was our leader who died yet is alive. The intrusion quality is the same—the places it shows up, the ubiquity. I wonder how I could have come so close without consciously having had the revelation. There are also the two contending demi-deities. Also, Runciter's messages are to make them aware of their true, unrecognized horrible condition—i.e., what their world is really made up of. It is made up of ice—resembling my first LSD experience. Is ice, too, an image, condition or symbol of the actual state of things: heat loss death (entropy)? And Ubik itself is warm. Could the Marxists have recognized _Ubik_ as a picture of Zebra and wondered if I [consciously] knew? Do _they_ know? It is their antagonist. Maybe they don't view it theologically but rather as a superior life form. (Maybe they are right.) This _would_ be scientific truth, as I told the Bureau. I conceive of Zebra as a weak "vegetable level" field, barely able to arrange matter. (Trigrams Sun and Li ~~.~~ ~~)~~ But its level (capacity to exert force) seems to be growing. To have thresholded recently. I have seen what it can do and have heard its voice. ***
quotes: wow—in _Stigmata_ Palmer Eldritch and Louis Bolero fight each other as did the two forces I saw noetically.
mentions.gloss: PKD is "staggered" to find *Stigmata* already dramatized his revelation: "Palmer Eldritch and Louis Bolero fight each other as did the two forces I saw noetically." The novel's two contending demi-deities become evidence that he wrote the war of God and anti-God before he consciously experienced it — Eldritch the dark counterpart to the salvific entity he finds in *Ubik*.

mentions.summary: Burroughs in _The Ticket That Exploded_ says of the Nova Mob parasites that as they move from one human host to another they give themselves away (to the Nova police) by the continuity of their _habits_ , such as tastes in food (in Hamburger Mary's case a taste for peanut butter). This was exactly true about Thomas. And I've subjectively felt myself as a female, a womb into which something like an egg (Firebright) was deposited—like a cuckoo egg. Was Thomas a saprophyte turned parasite, and deposited his "egg" in me? Does this mean that Burroughs is either intentionally or unintentionally describing something which is true? And he's into those pasted-together subliminal messages, too. KW has noted a resemblance between several things I've described and what Burroughs has written—e.g., my conviction that as a race or even planet we are "sick"—i.e., occluded perceptually, and that a divine doctor-entity is restoring us— Coincidence? Burroughs speaks of a virus—a word became a neural-cell virus, infecting us. After reading Burroughs, I dipped into _Ubik._ It certainly would be easy— and reasonable—for a reader to think that both Burroughs and I know something, and we want our novels to be taken as at least partly true. They have a strange ring of [revealed] truth about them—I feel it about his book, about mine—is, as Katherine Kurtz says, something writing _through_ us!? Isn't Palmer Eldritch a kind of parasite, replicating himself or itself using humans as hosts? But my sense about Thomas was of a benign, not evil, intrusion. Still, it was an intrusion into my psyche, a taking over. Are such intrusions always to be deplored? Or was I beguiled? Didn't it—he—get me out of trouble? There is just no doubt of it: such passages in Burroughs' novel as the "Do it—do it—neck" message within another message—words that weren't originally there but are like the inner trigrams of an _I Ching_ hex—that is one absolute "triangulated" element with (1) _Ubik_ and (2) what I saw in 3-7
quotes: Isn't Palmer Eldritch a kind of parasite, replicating himself or itself using humans as hosts?
mentions.gloss: Reading Burroughs on the Nova Mob's host-hopping parasites, PKD asks: "Isn't Palmer Eldritch a kind of parasite, replicating himself or itself using humans as hosts?" The stigmata-marked god is read as a predator that colonizes bodies. Crucially he turns the same suspicion on his own benign-seeming intrusion (Thomas) — "was I beguiled?" — using Eldritch as the figure for the fear that what possessed him was demonic, not divine.

mentions.summary: Insect characteristics: - (1) group mind ("hive of bees") - (2) metamorphosis of insect sort (chrysalis into final form) - (3) "neutral" (or "AI") voice ... dispassionate - (4) mimicry - (5) very old - (6) programming - (7) fierce mask (especially in O. Test) This "insect" metamorphosis which I saw is precisely that which God refers to when he says, "Look! I am building a new heaven and a new earth, and the memory of the former things ..." etc. In insect metamorphosis, contrasted to entelechy growth, you have a continual _breaking down_ of the old—which we do experience! This is precisely where the things we don't understand come in: pain, loss, stress. It is a moth—the luminous "moth" descending. And moths are precisely the life form which mimics (the Palmer Eldritch fearsome mask). What we call "time" is the metamorphosis—change of the moth as it passes from what it first was to what it will finally be. From our standpoint, it could reach its final state suddenly and unexpectedly _at any time_ —hence all the eschatological aspect of our religion. The parousia is very precisely the moment at which it _ends_ its in-time change process, its becoming, and abruptly _is_ (in final form). State one: the black iron prison Now: this middle world Later in time: the palm tree garden Finally: the sky and sea and Aphrodite world, which may be a primordial state lost (the fall) to which the metamorphosing moth is returning. Guess there really was a fall, so this metamorphosis is a repairing.
quotes: And moths are precisely the life form which mimics (the Palmer Eldritch fearsome mask).
mentions.gloss: The Eldritch mask becomes the type of deceptive mimicry within PKD's metamorphosis theology. Building his moth-and-chrysalis account of time and the parousia, he notes that "moths are precisely the life form which mimics (the Palmer Eldritch fearsome mask)." The novel's fearsome disguise supplies his image for a reality that masks its true form — the predatory face worn over the process of becoming.
